observed_before_amendment.allowed_prior_information: Only the v1 synthetic failures already recorded in the base protocol, source inspection, and unit/integrity tests that do not evaluate candidate performance.

reason: The base development feasibility rule constructs a provisional threshold from a development null sample and then evaluates false-alarm rate on that same sample. Because the threshold is itself a high empirical quantile of those nulls, the <=2% feasibility check is nearly guaranteed by construction and therefore does not provide an out-of-sample robustness screen.

The base protocol names a Huberized candidate but does not define a constant-baseline-invariant robust centering operation under heteroskedastic and correlated errors. Implementing one after seeing candidate results would create avoidable researcher degrees of freedom.

Several execution details that materially affect recovery or false alarms were not explicit: development signal sample size, signal-center law, reported-error vectors, AR(1) indexing semantics, outlier placement, and empirical quantile convention. They must be frozen before candidate evaluation.

candidate_statistics.rationale: Keep v2 as a comparison of the existing bank against one fully specified stability modification. A separately preregistered v3 may study robust residual transformations after defining their invariance and covariance semantics.

development_null_split.independence: Use distinct child RNG streams within the development seed namespace; no curve may appear in both halves.
development_null_split.provisional_threshold: For each candidate, estimate each regime's 0.995 quantile on the threshold-construction half using the higher empirical order-statistic convention; use the maximum regime threshold as the candidate's single provisional threshold.
development_null_split.feasibility: Apply the provisional threshold only to the independent feasibility-evaluation half. Reject a candidate if any regime has empirical false-alarm fraction >0.02.

development_signal_design.allocation_across_cadences: Exactly 10 paired signal/noise draws on each of the 25 frozen cadences for every family x width x signal-noise regime cell.
development_signal_design.center_distribution: Independent Uniform(0,60) days. Edge and seasonal-gap misses remain part of end-to-end recovery rather than being conditioned away.
development_signal_design.amplitude_definition: Positive unit-peak template multiplied by amplitude_sigma times the median reported error of that cadence.
development_signal_design.pairing: Every candidate and comparator receives the identical cadence, reported-error vector, noise draw, signal family, width, center, and amplitude.

reported_error_vectors.definition: One fixed vector per cadence; 64 independent Uniform(0.7,1.3) positive reported errors.
reported_error_vectors.seed_contract: Create SeedSequence(cadence_seed).spawn(50). Children 0..24 are reserved for the already locked cadence times; children 25..49 generate the reported-error vectors corresponding to cadence indices 0..24. The vectors are frozen before development and reused across all phases.
reported_error_vectors.purpose: Preserve the repository's existing moderate heteroskedasticity without letting error patterns vary across candidates or phases.

noise_generation_semantics.iid_gaussian: Independent N(0,1) residuals multiplied elementwise by the reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.ar1_rho: AR(1) correlation is by sorted observation index: Corr(i,j)=rho^abs(i-j), then scaled by reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.ou: Corr(i,j)=f*exp(-abs(t_i-t_j)/tau)+(1-f)*I(i=j), with f=0.8, then scaled by reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.errors_underestimated_factor_1_5: Independent Gaussian residuals with true standard deviation 1.5 times the reported error while the search continues to receive the uninflated reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.student_t3_unit_variance: Independent Student-t(3)/sqrt(3) residuals multiplied by reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.variance_doubles_second_half: Independent Gaussian noise with variance multiplier 2 for epochs with time >30 days, i.e. standard-deviation multiplier sqrt(2).
noise_generation_semantics.single_positive_outlier: Start from IID Gaussian noise and choose one epoch uniformly at random; add the named positive sigma amplitude times that epoch's reported error.
noise_generation_semantics.two_positive_5sigma_outliers: Start from IID Gaussian noise and sample two distinct epoch indices uniformly without replacement; add +5 times each selected epoch's reported error.
noise_generation_semantics.contaminated_gaussian_sigma8: Independently per epoch, use N(0,1) with probability 0.99 and N(0,8^2) with probability 0.01, then multiply by reported errors.
noise_generation_semantics.linear_variance_drift: Independent Gaussian noise with variance multiplier changing linearly from 0.75 at day 0 to 1.75 at day 60; standard deviation is the square root of that multiplier times the reported error.

quantile_convention.rule: Every 0.995 empirical calibration quantile uses the higher order-statistic convention (equivalent to numpy.quantile(values,0.995,method='higher')).
quantile_convention.threshold_comparison: A curve is counted as detected when statistic >= the frozen threshold.
quantile_convention.ties: Report the number of calibration values exactly equal to each regime threshold; do not jitter ties.

execution_rule: All v2 development runners must verify both the original base-protocol lock and this amendment before generating any candidate-performance statistic. The original base protocol remains immutable in the artifact bundle.
